commands.title: Read a manual page
commands.description: Opens the full manual for a command. Press q to leave it.

commands.title: Show command help
commands.description: Shows a command's built-in summary and its available flags.

commands.title: Search manual topics
commands.description: Finds manual pages whose names or summaries mention a topic.

commands.title: Explain a command name
commands.description: Says whether a name is an executable, alias, function, or shell built-in.

commands.title: Find a command file
commands.description: Prints the executable file your shell would run for a command name.

commands.title: Read practical examples
commands.description: Shows a short community-written page of common examples.

commands.title: Show the current folder
commands.description: Prints the full path of the folder you are in.

commands.title: List every file
commands.description: Lists files with details. -a includes hidden names and -l shows permissions, owners, sizes, and dates.

commands.title: Enter a folder
commands.description: Makes a folder your current working location.

commands.title: Return to the last folder
commands.description: Switches back to the previous working folder.

commands.title: Go to your home folder
commands.description: Moves to your personal home folder from anywhere.

commands.title: Go up one folder
commands.description: Moves to the folder that contains the current one.

commands.title: List readable file sizes
commands.description: Lists file details with sizes such as KiB and MiB instead of raw bytes.

commands.title: Show a folder tree
commands.description: Draws folders and files two levels deep. -L controls the depth.

commands.title: Copy a file
commands.description: Copies one file to a new name or folder.

commands.title: Copy a folder
commands.description: Copies a folder and everything inside it. -r means recursive.

commands.title: Move or rename a file
commands.description: Moves an item to another folder or gives it a new name.

commands.title: Create nested folders
commands.description: Creates the requested folder and any missing parent folders. -p also avoids an error when they already exist.

commands.title: Create an empty file
commands.description: Creates an empty file, or updates the date on an existing one.

commands.title: Create a symbolic link
commands.description: Creates a link that points to another file or folder. -s makes the link symbolic instead of a hard link.

commands.title: Measure a folder
commands.description: Shows one human-readable total for a folder. -s summarizes and -h formats the size.

commands.title: Inspect file details
commands.description: Shows exact size, permissions, ownership, and timestamps for a file.

commands.title: Identify a file type
commands.description: Examines a file's contents and reports its likely format.

commands.title: Delete a file
commands.description: Deletes a file immediately without using the desktop trash. Check the path before pressing Enter.

commands.title: Delete a folder tree
commands.description: Deletes a folder and everything below it without using the trash. -r follows the whole tree, so a wrong path can erase a lot of data.

commands.title: Force-delete a folder tree
commands.description: Deletes a folder tree without confirmation and ignores missing files. -f removes safeguards, so verify the expanded path first.

commands.title: Resolve a full path
commands.description: Prints an absolute path with symbolic links and relative parts resolved.

commands.title: Print a text file
commands.description: Prints a whole text file to the terminal. Use less for long files.

commands.title: Page through a text file
commands.description: Opens a scrollable reader. Use / to search and q to leave.

commands.title: Read the first lines
commands.description: Prints the first 20 lines. -n sets how many lines to show.

commands.title: Follow new file lines
commands.description: Prints the end of a file and waits for new lines. -f keeps following until Ctrl+C.

commands.title: Edit a text file
commands.description: Opens a beginner-friendly terminal editor. The shortcut bar at the bottom uses ^ for Ctrl.

commands.title: Count lines
commands.description: Counts newline-separated lines in a file. -l selects the line count.

commands.title: Compare two files
commands.description: Shows changed lines in a readable patch. -u includes surrounding context.

commands.title: Sort text lines
commands.description: Prints the lines in alphabetical order without changing the file.

commands.title: Remove repeated lines
commands.description: Sorts the input, then prints one copy of each adjacent repeated line.

commands.title: Select a text column
commands.description: Prints one field from each line. -d sets the separator and -f chooses the field number.

commands.title: Save piped output
commands.description: Shows a command's output while also saving it to a file.

commands.title: Number text lines
commands.description: Prints every line with a number. -b a includes blank lines.

commands.title: Find files by name
commands.description: Searches below a folder for names containing the text. -iname ignores letter case.

commands.title: Find large files
commands.description: Finds regular files larger than 100 MiB. Change 100M to the size you need.

commands.title: Find recently changed files
commands.description: Finds regular files changed during the last seven days. -mtime -7 means newer than seven days.

commands.title: Search text in a folder
commands.description: Searches files recursively and prints matching line numbers. -r recurses and -n adds the line number.

commands.title: Search without letter case
commands.description: Finds matching lines while treating uppercase and lowercase as equal. -i enables that behavior.

commands.title: Search project text quickly
commands.description: Searches text recursively, respects ignore files, and prints useful line context. Ryoku installs ripgrep by default.

commands.title: Find names quickly
commands.description: Searches file and folder names with simple patterns and respects ignore files. Ryoku installs fd by default.

commands.title: Find empty items
commands.description: Finds empty files and folders below a location.

commands.title: Find executable files
commands.description: Finds regular files your current user is allowed to execute.

commands.title: Run one command as root
commands.description: Runs one command with administrator permission after authenticating. Read the command carefully before approving it.

commands.title: Make a file executable
commands.description: Adds permission to run a script or program as your user.

commands.title: Set normal file permissions
commands.description: Lets the owner read and write while everyone else can only read. This is a common mode for ordinary files.

commands.title: Set executable permissions
commands.description: Lets the owner read, write, and execute while everyone else can read and execute.

commands.title: Change an item's owner
commands.description: Changes the owning user and group of one item. This can block access if the names are wrong.

commands.title: Edit a protected file safely
commands.description: Edits a protected file through your normal editor, then installs the result with administrator permission.

commands.title: Open a root login shell
commands.description: Starts an administrator shell with root's environment. Every command is privileged until you run exit.

commands.title: Show the permission mask
commands.description: Shows which permission bits the shell removes when new files and folders are created.

commands.title: Show numeric owners
commands.description: Lists permission bits plus numeric user and group IDs, which helps diagnose unknown owners.

commands.title: Open every permission
commands.description: Gives every user full access throughout a folder tree. This destroys useful security boundaries and is almost never the right fix.

commands.title: Install a repository package
commands.description: Downloads and installs a package from configured repositories. -S synchronizes the requested package and dependencies.

commands.title: Remove a package and leftovers
commands.description: Removes a package, unused dependencies, and its system configuration backups. Review the transaction before accepting it.

commands.title: Search repository packages
commands.description: Searches package names and descriptions in configured repositories.

commands.title: Inspect a repository package
commands.description: Shows a repository package's version, size, description, dependencies, and source.

commands.title: List installed packages
commands.description: Lists every installed package and its version.

commands.title: Find which package owns a file
commands.description: Reports which installed package supplied a file.

commands.title: List chosen packages
commands.description: Lists packages installed explicitly rather than only as dependencies.

commands.title: List orphaned packages
commands.description: Lists dependencies that are no longer required by another installed package. Inspect them before removing anything.

commands.title: Trim the package cache
commands.description: Keeps the newest three cached versions of each package and deletes older copies. -r performs the removal.

commands.title: Check for system updates
commands.description: Lists repository updates without changing the live package database.

commands.title: Update the base system directly
commands.description: Refreshes package databases and upgrades the Arch or CachyOS base. Prefer ryoku update --system so Ryoku and the system update together with snapshot protection.

commands.title: Install an AUR package
commands.description: Builds and installs a package from the AUR or normal repositories. Read the build files and prompts before accepting them.

commands.title: Search the AUR
commands.description: Searches both normal repositories and the user-maintained AUR.

commands.title: Install a Fedora package
commands.description: Installs a package and its dependencies from configured Fedora repositories.

commands.title: Remove a Fedora package
commands.description: Removes a package and dependencies no longer needed by anything else. Review the transaction before accepting it.

commands.title: Search Fedora packages
commands.description: Searches package names and summaries in configured repositories.

commands.title: Inspect a Fedora package
commands.description: Shows a package's version, source repository, size, and description.

commands.title: List installed Fedora packages
commands.description: Lists installed packages with their versions and source repositories.

commands.title: Find a file's Fedora package
commands.description: Searches enabled repositories for the package that supplies a file path.

commands.title: List chosen Fedora packages
commands.description: Lists packages marked as installed by the user rather than pulled in only as dependencies.

commands.title: List unneeded Fedora packages
commands.description: Lists installed packages no longer needed by user-installed software. Inspect the list before removing anything.

commands.title: Clear downloaded Fedora packages
commands.description: Deletes cached package files while keeping repository metadata.

commands.title: Update Fedora directly
commands.description: Refreshes metadata and upgrades the Fedora base. Prefer ryoku update --system so Ryoku and the system update together; Fedora does not provide Ryoku snapshot rollback.

commands.title: Install a Void package
commands.description: Refreshes repository indexes and installs a package with its dependencies. -S synchronizes the indexes first.

commands.title: Remove a Void package
commands.description: Removes a package and dependencies that no other package needs. Review the transaction before accepting it.

commands.title: Search Void packages
commands.description: Searches names and descriptions in remote repositories. -R uses repository data and -s searches it.

commands.title: Inspect a Void package
commands.description: Shows information about a package available from configured repositories.

commands.title: List installed Void packages
commands.description: Lists every installed package and its version.

commands.title: Find a file's Void package
commands.description: Reports which installed package owns a file path.

commands.title: List chosen Void packages
commands.description: Lists packages marked as manually installed rather than pulled in only as dependencies.

commands.title: List orphaned Void packages
commands.description: Lists installed packages that are no longer required. Inspect the list before removing anything.

commands.title: Clean the XBPS cache
commands.description: Deletes obsolete package files from the XBPS cache. -O targets cached packages that are no longer installed or available.

commands.title: Update Void directly
commands.description: Refreshes repositories and upgrades the Void base. Prefer ryoku update --system because direct XBPS updates do not receive Ryoku's pre/post snapshots.

commands.title: Search Flatpak apps
commands.description: Searches configured Flatpak remotes for desktop apps and runtimes.

commands.title: Install a Flatpak app
commands.description: Installs an app from Flathub for the current system. Confirm the app ID and requested permissions.

commands.title: List Flatpak apps
commands.description: Lists installed Flatpak applications without listing their shared runtimes.

commands.title: Update Flatpak apps
commands.description: Downloads available updates for installed Flatpak apps and runtimes.

commands.title: Remove a Flatpak app
commands.description: Removes one Flatpak app after showing what will change. Its personal app data remains unless you add --delete-data.

commands.title: Check a system service
commands.description: Shows whether a service is running plus its latest status messages.

commands.title: Restart a system service
commands.description: Stops and starts a service now. Active connections or work handled by it may be interrupted.

commands.title: Start a system service
commands.description: Starts a service for the current boot without enabling future boots.

commands.title: Stop a system service
commands.description: Stops a running service until something starts it again.

commands.title: Enable a service at boot
commands.description: Starts a service now and configures it to start on later boots. --now performs both actions.

commands.title: Disable a boot service
commands.description: Stops a service now and prevents its automatic start on later boots.

commands.title: List failed services
commands.description: Lists system services that entered a failed state during this boot.

commands.title: Read a service log
commands.description: Shows this boot's journal entries for one service. -u selects the unit and -b limits output to the current boot.

commands.title: Follow a service log
commands.description: Shows recent entries for one service and waits for new ones. -f follows and -u selects the unit.

commands.title: Read this boot's log
commands.description: Shows warning-or-higher journal messages from the current boot. -p sets the minimum priority.

commands.title: Check a Void service
commands.description: Shows whether a supervised Void system service is running and for how long.

commands.title: Restart a Void service
commands.description: Stops and starts a supervised Void service. Active work handled by it may be interrupted.

commands.title: Start a Void service
commands.description: Asks runit to start an already enabled system service.

commands.title: Stop a Void service
commands.description: Stops a supervised service and keeps it down until it is brought up again.

commands.title: Enable a Void service
commands.description: Links a service definition into the active runit service directory so it starts now and on later boots.

commands.title: Disable a Void service
commands.description: Removes the activation link so runit stops supervising the service. A wrong path can delete something other than the intended link.

commands.title: Check a Void user service
commands.description: Shows the state of a Turnstile-managed service belonging to your login session.

commands.title: Follow the Void system log
commands.description: Follows the combined socklog stream under /var/log/socklog. Stop following with Ctrl+C.

commands.title: Follow Void daemon logs
commands.description: Follows daemon messages collected by socklog under /var/log/socklog.

commands.title: List running processes
commands.description: Shows processes for all users with CPU, memory, start time, and full command details.

commands.title: Open the process monitor
commands.description: Opens Ryoku's interactive CPU, memory, disk, network, and process monitor. Press q to leave.

commands.title: Monitor processes live
commands.description: Shows a continuously updated process table using the standard system tool. Press q to leave.

commands.title: Find process IDs by name
commands.description: Finds matching process IDs and full command lines. -a prints the command and -f searches all of it.

commands.title: Ask a process to stop
commands.description: Sends the normal termination signal so a process can save state and clean up.

commands.title: Stop processes by name
commands.description: Sends the normal termination signal to every matching process name. Check matches with pgrep first.

commands.title: Force a process to stop
commands.description: Stops a process immediately with no chance to save or clean up. Use -9 only when normal termination has failed.

commands.title: Start with lower CPU priority
commands.description: Starts a command with less CPU scheduling priority. Larger nice values yield more readily to other work.

commands.title: Lower a running priority
commands.description: Changes a running process to nice value 10. -p says the following number is a process ID.

commands.title: Show uptime and system load
commands.description: Shows how long the system has run and its one, five, and fifteen minute load averages.

commands.title: Show the kernel version
commands.description: Prints the version and build name of the running Linux kernel.

commands.title: Summarize this computer
commands.description: Shows a compact Ryoku system summary including the OS, kernel, desktop, CPU, GPU, and memory.

commands.title: Inspect the processor
commands.description: Shows CPU model, architecture, core counts, virtualization, and supported features.

commands.title: Show memory use
commands.description: Shows used and available memory and swap. -h formats values in readable units.

commands.title: List disks and partitions
commands.description: Shows storage devices, partitions, sizes, and mount points as a tree.

commands.title: List PCI hardware and drivers
commands.description: Lists internal PCI devices and the kernel drivers attached to them. -k adds driver details.

commands.title: List USB devices
commands.description: Lists attached USB devices with their vendor and product identifiers.

commands.title: Read hardware temperatures
commands.description: Shows temperatures, fan speeds, and voltages exposed by supported hardware sensors.

commands.title: Show the computer identity
commands.description: Shows the hostname, operating system, architecture, and kernel reported by the system manager.

commands.title: Show the Void hostname
commands.description: Prints the computer's current network name.

commands.title: Show edition information
commands.description: Prints the operating system's machine-readable name, version, and family information.

commands.title: Read kernel messages
commands.description: Shows kernel messages from the current boot through the system journal. -k selects kernel entries and -b selects this boot.

commands.title: Read the kernel ring buffer
commands.description: Shows kernel and hardware messages with readable timestamps. Administrator permission may be required by the running security policy.

commands.title: Show disk space
commands.description: Shows used and available space on mounted filesystems. -h formats sizes in readable units.

commands.title: List filesystem details
commands.description: Shows disks and partitions with filesystem types, labels, UUIDs, and mount points.

commands.title: Show mounted filesystems
commands.description: Shows the mount tree with each source device, target folder, and filesystem type.

commands.title: Mount a filesystem
commands.description: Attaches a device's filesystem at an existing folder. Confirm the device and target before mounting.

commands.title: Unmount a filesystem
commands.description: Detaches a mounted filesystem after pending writes finish. Close files and terminals using it first.

commands.title: Mount a removable drive
commands.description: Mounts a removable block device through the desktop storage service. -b identifies the device path.

commands.title: Inspect partition tables
commands.description: Lists disks, partitions, sector ranges, and partition types without changing them.

commands.title: Show Btrfs allocation
commands.description: Shows detailed data, metadata, and free-space allocation for Ryoku's Btrfs root filesystem.

commands.title: Summarize Btrfs space
commands.description: Summarizes how Ryoku's Btrfs root divides space between data, metadata, and system blocks.

commands.title: List system snapshots
commands.description: Lists Btrfs snapshots, their dates, types, and descriptions. Ryoku uses them for update recovery on supported editions.

commands.title: Show filesystem identifiers
commands.description: Lists device UUIDs, labels, and filesystem types used by mount configuration.

commands.title: Write an image to a drive
commands.command: sudo dd if=<image-file> of=<device> bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync
commands.description: Copies an image byte-for-byte onto a device and waits for writes to finish. A wrong of= device destroys its existing data and partition table.

commands.title: Create a filesystem
commands.description: Formats a device as ext4. Formatting destroys the filesystem and files already on that device.

commands.title: Show network addresses
commands.description: Lists network interfaces and their IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

commands.title: Show network routes
commands.description: Shows where IPv4 traffic is sent, including the default gateway.

commands.title: Test network reachability
commands.description: Sends four test packets and reports delay and packet loss. -c 4 stops after four replies or timeouts.

commands.title: List nearby Wi-Fi networks
commands.description: Asks Ryoku's default NetworkManager service to scan and list nearby wireless networks.

commands.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
commands.description: Connects through NetworkManager and prompts for the password without placing it in shell history. --ask requests missing secrets interactively.

commands.title: Show saved connections
commands.description: Lists NetworkManager connection profiles and marks the ones currently active.

commands.title: Show active DNS servers
commands.description: Shows the IPv4 DNS servers NetworkManager assigned to active devices.

commands.title: Show listening services
commands.description: Lists listening TCP and UDP ports with owning processes. -t and -u select protocols, -l listeners, -p processes, and -n numeric addresses.

commands.title: Download a file with curl
commands.description: Downloads a URL using its remote filename. -L follows redirects and -O keeps that filename.

commands.title: Download a file with wget
commands.description: Downloads a URL to the current folder and shows progress.

commands.title: Open a remote shell
commands.description: Opens an encrypted terminal session on another computer. Verify a new host fingerprint before accepting it.

commands.title: Copy a file securely
commands.description: Copies a file to another computer over an encrypted SSH connection.

commands.title: Sync files to another computer
commands.description: Copies changed files over SSH while preserving useful metadata. -a preserves the tree, -v reports work, and -h formats sizes.

commands.title: Show your public address
commands.description: Asks an external service which public IP address your connection uses.

commands.title: Trace a network path
commands.description: Shows the network hops toward a host and helps locate routing or MTU problems.

commands.title: Create a tar archive
commands.description: Packs a folder into one uncompressed archive. -c creates and -f names the archive file.

commands.title: Extract a tar archive
commands.description: Extracts an archive into the current folder. -x extracts and -f selects the archive file.

commands.title: List a tar archive
commands.description: Lists archive contents without extracting them. -t lists and -f selects the archive file.

commands.title: Create a compressed tarball
commands.description: Packs a folder and compresses it with gzip. -z enables gzip compression.

commands.title: Extract a gzip tarball
commands.description: Decompresses a gzip tarball and extracts its files into the current folder.

commands.title: Compress one file with gzip
commands.description: Creates a .gz copy and keeps the original file. -k means keep the input.

commands.title: Compress one file with zstd
commands.description: Creates a fast .zst compressed copy and keeps the original file.

commands.title: Create a ZIP archive
commands.description: Creates a ZIP containing a folder tree. -r includes everything below the folder.

commands.title: Extract a ZIP archive
commands.description: Extracts a ZIP into the folder named after -d.

commands.title: Extract a 7-Zip archive
commands.description: Extracts an archive while preserving its folder structure. x selects full-path extraction.

commands.title: Show your user name
commands.description: Prints the effective user name of the current shell.

commands.title: Show user and group IDs
commands.description: Shows your numeric user ID, primary group, and supplementary groups.

commands.title: List your groups
commands.description: Lists the groups that grant your account access to files and system features.

commands.title: Change your password
commands.description: Prompts for your current password and then a new login password without showing either on screen.

commands.title: Add a user to a group
commands.description: Adds a user to a supplementary group. -a keeps existing memberships and -G names the added groups; the user must log in again.

commands.title: Switch to another user
commands.description: Starts a login shell as another user after asking for that account's password. The dash loads the target user's environment.

commands.title: Show logged-in users
commands.description: Lists current login sessions, terminals, and login times.

commands.title: Look up an account
commands.description: Shows the system account record, including its user ID, home folder, and login shell.

commands.title: Show command history
commands.description: Lists commands remembered by your current bash, zsh, or fish session.

commands.title: Search command history
commands.description: Starts an interactive backward search through earlier commands. Keep pressing Ctrl+R for older matches.

commands.title: Pipe output to another command
commands.description: Sends the first command's output into the second command as input.

commands.title: Write output to a file
commands.description: Replaces a file with a command's normal output. An existing file is overwritten without confirmation.

commands.title: Append output to a file
commands.description: Adds a command's normal output to the end of a file instead of replacing it.

commands.title: Save output and errors
commands.description: Writes normal output to a file, then sends error output to the same place. The file is replaced.

commands.title: Run only after success
commands.description: Runs the second command only when the first exits successfully.

commands.title: Create a command alias
commands.description: Creates a short name for this bash or zsh session. In fish, use alias ll 'ls -la'.

commands.title: Set a value for one command
commands.description: Sets an environment variable for one bash or zsh command. In fish, use env NAME=value <command>.

commands.title: Export an environment value
commands.description: Makes a value available to later commands from this bash or zsh session. In fish, use set -gx NAME value.

commands.title: Add a command folder to PATH
commands.description: Puts a folder first in bash or zsh's executable search path for this session. In fish, use fish_add_path ~/.local/bin.

commands.title: Reload shell configuration
commands.description: Loads bash configuration into the current shell; zsh uses ~/.zshrc. Fish uses source ~/.config/fish/config.fish.

commands.title: Run a command in the background
commands.description: Starts a command as a background job so the terminal can accept more input.

commands.title: List shell jobs
commands.description: Lists background and suspended jobs owned by the current shell.

commands.title: Bring a job to the foreground
commands.description: Returns a background or suspended job to the terminal. Use jobs to find its number.

commands.title: Interrupt a running command
commands.description: Sends an interrupt signal to the foreground command, which normally asks it to stop.

commands.title: Suspend a running command
commands.description: Pauses the foreground command and returns control to the shell. Use fg to continue it.

commands.title: Lock the current session
commands.description: Asks the login manager to lock your active desktop session.

commands.title: Suspend the computer
commands.description: Asks the system manager to save the session in memory and enter sleep. Save open work first.

commands.title: Suspend Void
commands.description: Asks Void's elogind login manager to suspend the computer. Save open work first.

commands.title: End the current session
commands.description: Ends your current login session and closes its applications. Save open work first.

commands.title: Restart the computer
commands.description: Asks the system manager to close the session and reboot. Save open work first.

commands.title: Shut down the computer
commands.description: Asks the system manager to close the session and turn off the computer. Save open work first.

commands.title: Restart Void
commands.description: Asks runit to stop services and reboot the computer. Save open work first.

commands.title: Shut down Void
commands.description: Asks runit to stop services and turn off the computer. Save open work first.

commands.title: List login sessions
commands.description: Lists active local and remote login sessions with their user and seat.

commands.title: Clone a repository
commands.description: Downloads a repository and its history into a new folder.

commands.title: Show repository status
commands.description: Shows the current branch and which files are changed, staged, or untracked.

commands.title: Review unstaged changes
commands.description: Shows line-by-line changes that have not been staged yet.

commands.title: Stage a file
commands.description: Adds the current version of one file to the next commit.

commands.title: Review staged changes
commands.description: Shows exactly what the next commit will contain.

commands.title: Commit staged changes
commands.description: Records the staged changes with a short message. -m supplies that message on the command line.

commands.title: Read compact history
commands.description: Shows the newest 20 commits as one line each with branch and tag names.

commands.title: Pull remote changes
commands.description: Downloads and fast-forwards the current branch. --ff-only stops instead of creating an unexpected merge commit.

commands.title: Push local commits
commands.description: Uploads commits from the current branch to its configured remote branch.

commands.title: List branches
commands.description: Lists local and remote-tracking branches. The current branch has an asterisk.

commands.title: Switch branches
commands.description: Checks out an existing branch in the working folder.

commands.title: Create and switch branches
commands.description: Creates a branch at the current commit and switches to it. -c means create.

commands.title: Discard changes to a file
commands.description: Replaces an unstaged file with the committed version. Uncommitted changes in that file are lost.

commands.title: Unstage a file
commands.description: Removes a file from the next commit while keeping its working changes.

commands.title: Inspect a commit
commands.description: Shows one commit's message, metadata, and patch.

commands.title: Replace remote branch history
commands.description: Rewrites the remote branch only if it has not moved since your last fetch. It can still erase shared history, so coordinate before using it.
